steps.title: The Opening Question
steps.content:
So {{contact_first_name}}, how have things been since {{pt_you}} finished the aligners with us? I usually hear one of three things. Still holding straight, a little shifting starting, or moved back quite a bit. Which one is closest?

(Only three answers. Tap the one you hear.)

steps.title: Still Holding Straight
steps.content:
That's great to hear, {{contact_first_name}}. That's the retainer doing its job, and it means the work {{pt_you}} put in is still paying off. A straight smile that stays straight is the whole goal.

(Let them enjoy it. Then ask permission for the questions.)

steps.title: A Little Shifting
steps.content:
That's common, {{contact_first_name}}. Teeth want to drift back toward where they started, especially when retainer wear slips, and {{pt_no_fault}}. It's the reason we check in. When shifting is caught early, it's usually much easier to correct. What do you think made it start, the retainers wearing out or life getting busy?

(Let them answer. Do not try to book yet.)

steps.title: Moved Back Quite a Bit
steps.content:
That's common, {{contact_first_name}}, and please don't feel bad. Teeth want to drift back toward where they started once the retainer routine slips, and {{pt_no_fault}}. It's the reason we check in. Your notes say {{pt_you}} finished with a smile to be proud of. What do you think made it come back, the retainers wearing out or life getting busy?

(Let them answer. Stay warm. Do not try to book yet.)

steps.title: Ask Permission for the Questions
steps.content:
While I have you, {{contact_first_name}}, can I ask a few quick questions about how the teeth are holding up? They move so slowly that nobody catches it happening.

(Wait for the yes.)

steps.title: Ask Permission for the Questions
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, we'll come back to the shifting in a moment. First, can I ask a few quick questions so {{pt_your_file}} is up to date?

(Wait for the yes.)

steps.title: The Questions: Update the File
steps.content:
(Write down everything they mention. You'll recap it in a moment.)

First, the shifting. Is it mostly the front teeth, or crowding coming back?

How about the retainers, still going in at night, or has the routine slipped a little?

Any changes in {{pt_your}} bite, like teeth hitting differently or chewing more on one side?

How about flossing, any tight spots where the floss catches or shreds?

Any jaw soreness, clicking, or headaches in the morning?

How does {{pt_your}} smile feel in photos these days, still showing it off?

Finally, anything the dentist has flagged since we last saw {{pt_them}}?

(Recap what you wrote down, including the shifting, then ask:)

{{contact_first_name}}, between the shifting and anything else you mentioned, which one would you most like to take care of?

(If the shifting is the only thing on the list, that's the answer. Tap the button and continue.)

steps.title: The Questions: Update the File
steps.content:
(Write down everything they mention. You'll recap it in a moment.)

First, any shifting or crowding at all since the aligners came off, even something small?

How about the retainers, still going in at night, or has the routine slipped a little?

Any changes in {{pt_your}} bite, like teeth hitting differently or chewing more on one side?

How about flossing, any tight spots where the floss catches or shreds?

Any jaw soreness, clicking, or headaches in the morning?

How does {{pt_your}} smile feel in photos these days, still showing it off?

Finally, anything the dentist has flagged since we last saw {{pt_them}}?

(Recap what you wrote down, then ask:)

{{contact_first_name}}, of those, which one would you most like to take care of?

(Tap their answer below. If nothing came up, that's still a good call. Use the second button.)

steps.title: Making It Real
steps.content:
(Ask these three questions in order. Pause after each and let them answer.)

How long has it been on {{pt_your}} mind, like a few weeks, or longer than that?

(Let them answer.)

Is it something that comes up now and then, or every time {{pt_your}} smile is in a photo?

(Let them answer.)

When it's at its worst, does it ever interfere with photos, smiling around people, or {{pt_your}} confidence?

(Let them answer. Repeat back whatever they name.)

Thank you for sharing that. It makes sense, and it's something we help people with all the time.

steps.title: The Review
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, let me make sure I have this right.

(Read back their three answers: how long, how often, what it gets in the way of.)

So it's been on {{pt_your}} mind a while, and it comes up most times there's a photo. At its worst it gets in the way of what you mentioned. Did I get that right?

(Say what they named: photos, smiling around people, or {{pt_your}} confidence. Let them answer. If they correct you, take the correction and move on.)

And it sounds like you'd love to see {{pt_them}} showing off that smile again without a second thought. Is that fair to say?

(Most people say yes. Tap what you hear.)

steps.title: The Recommendation
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, that's worth getting looked at instead of just dealing with it. A quick scan shows us where the teeth stand compared to where {{pt_you}} finished. If it's minor, a refreshed retainer or a short refinement is often all it takes. If everything is holding better than you think, we'll tell you that too. Does that make sense?

(Wait for the yes.)

{{contact_first_name}}, can I make a recommendation?

(Wait for the yes.)

Let's {{pt_get_you_in}} for that quick scan, so {{provider_name}} can take a look at {{main_concern}}. Does that sound reasonable?

(Say "does that sound reasonable", not "does that sound good". Tap what you hear.)

steps.title: They Hesitate: Find Out Why
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, I don't want to assume anything. Is it the timing, or is something else holding you back?

(Stay easy about it. No pressure. Let them answer.)

steps.title: Nothing Found: The Retainer Check
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, I'm glad everything is in good shape.

One thing before I let you go. Even when everything feels like it's holding, retainers age. They stretch, warp, and wear thin, and teeth take advantage of that. A quick check with a current scan makes sure everything is holding where it should. If the retainers need refreshing, we handle it right there. Does that make sense?

(Wait for the yes.)

{{contact_first_name}}, can I make a recommendation?

(Wait for the yes.)

Let's {{pt_get_you_in}} so we can check those retainers and keep that smile where it belongs. Does that sound reasonable?

steps.title: Scheduling: Two Options
steps.content:
Wonderful, {{contact_first_name}}. We have times this week on (day) and (day). Do mornings or afternoons work better for you?

(Let them answer.)

Perfect, I have (time) and (time). Which is better?

(Let them answer.)

Great, I have you down for (day) at (time).

(Always offer two options within 48 hours. Know your two days and two times before the call. Once booked, add your notes and press the green "Scheduled" button below to log the call.)

steps.title: Parent Mode
steps.content: (Parent mode is on. Every screen from here uses parent or guardian wording automatically.)

steps.title: Objection: “Start all over?”
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, that's the number one worry, and the answer is usually not. When shifting is caught early, it's often a short refinement, a handful of trays instead of a whole new treatment. The scan tells us where things stand, so you know what it would take before deciding anything.

(Do not quote prices or promise treatment lengths on the call. The scan determines that.)

Does that make sense?

(Wait for the yes.)

steps.title: Objection: The retainer routine slipped
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, please don't be. There's no judgment here. Teeth drift back the moment the retainer routine slips. That's how teeth behave, and {{pt_no_fault}}. It's the reason we check in, and we'd like to help {{pt_them}} protect that smile.

Would you be open to that?

(Wait for the yes.)

steps.title: Objection: “I need to think about it”
steps.content:
That's fair, {{contact_first_name}}. Can I ask what part you'd want to think over? Sometimes it's the cost, sometimes the timing, and sometimes people just want to be sure it's the right move.

(Listen. Their answer usually points to one of the other objections. If it stays general, keep going.)

Coming in is really just information. You'd find out what the options look like and what it would involve, and then you decide with real answers. If it's not the right fit, we'll tell you that too.

Does that help?

steps.title: Objection: “Just send me some info”
steps.content:
I'd be glad to send you some information, {{contact_first_name}}. The one thing I'd say is that a flyer can only tell you so much. It can't look at {{pt_your}} teeth. That's what the visit is for. So let me get you on the schedule first, and then I'll send the information along.

Is that okay?
